Alice.summary: Property under the Criminal Act is an object with monetary value, regardless of whether ownership and transfer are lawful.

Bob.summary: Property under the Criminal Act is an object for which the owner's intention to possess is expressed, regardless of monetary value or lawful ownership.

Charlie.summary: Property under the Criminal Act requires both monetary exchange value and lawful ownership and transfer.

c1.text: Under the Criminal Act, 'property' refers to an object with economic value.

c2.text: Economic value means pure economic value, that is, monetary value.

c3.text: Under the Criminal Act, property is irrelevant to whether the ownership and transfer of the object are lawful.

c4.text: An object with monetary value is property under the Criminal Act, regardless of whether its ownership and transfer are lawful.

c5.text: Economic value is subjectively attached by the owner.

c6.text: Property does not necessarily have to be lawfully owned or lawfully traded.

c7.text: As long as the owner's intention to possess is expressed, the object is property under the Criminal Act, regardless of whether there is monetary exchange value.

c8.text: Monetary exchange value is a necessary condition for economic value to be recognized.

c9.text: In order for something to be property under the Criminal Act, its ownership and transfer must be lawful.

c10.text: An object is property under the Criminal Act only if it has monetary exchange value and its ownership and transfer are lawful.

a.note: Alice requires only monetary value and considers lawful ownership irrelevant, so she regards narcotics as property.

b.note: Bob considers subjective attachment and expressed intention to possess sufficient, so he regards both items as property.

c.note: Charlie requires both monetary exchange value and lawful ownership/transfer. The fan letter lacks monetary exchange value, so Charlie does not regard it as property.

h1.text: Narcotics are illegally owned by a drug dealer and prohibited by law from being owned.

h3.text: The drug dealer has expressed an intention to possess the narcotics.

h4.text: Narcotics illegally owned by a drug dealer are property under the Criminal Act.

h5.text: Narcotics illegally owned by a drug dealer are not property under the Criminal Act.

h6.text: A fan letter cherished by a celebrity is not subject to transaction and has no monetary exchange value.

h7.text: The celebrity expresses an intention to possess the cherished fan letter.

h8.text: A fan letter cherished by a celebrity is property under the Criminal Act.

h9.text: A fan letter cherished by a celebrity is not property under the Criminal Act.
